parsed.explanation: The operative regime combines a statutory binary-sex facilities rule reaching restrooms, locker rooms, dormitories, shelters and prisons with no working remedy, a border posture that lets officers refuse cases over sex-document doubt and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility, and documented state-perpetrated harm in custody (conversion-style practices for trans inmates; forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse of trans men in immigration detention). Counterterrorism language frames pro-transgender advocacy as a priority target. Mitigating: no criminalisation of trans identity, a national gender-identity hate-crime statute, active litigation enjoining several measures, and no documented enforcement of this state's facilities statute — so the result sits at the top of High Risk rather than lower.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules recognise only M/F; officers instructed to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex and to weigh lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected misrepresentation of sex; trans athletes barred; eight governments issued traveller advisories; detentions of foreign nationals over visa issues reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements and is never automatic; passport policy under active litigation and a legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign visitor's home-issued marker meets a screening posture primed to treat discrepancy as possible deception, escalating to refusal, secondary evidence demands, or permanent ineligibility.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies for trans inmates (forced haircuts, HRT removal, psychiatric substitution); trans men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; trans prisoner counts no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders enjoined in litigation; custodial protections for trans prisoners rescinded. No documented consular-access safeguard for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or immigration hold converts a document or facilities dispute into birth-sex custody with documented state-perpetrated harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State statute defines sex as binary at birth and reaches bathrooms, locker rooms, dormitories, rape crisis centres and prisons; a religious-refusal statute permits service and housing denial with qualified immunity; four states criminalise trans facility use by trespass; a trans student was arrested and held in a men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Fifteen city ordinances bar gender-identity discrimination (nullification bill pending); national gender-identity hate-crime statute; courts have blocked some national measures.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exclusion is universal exposure for every outed visitor, with no state remedy; local ordinances are the only counterweight and are under legislative attack.

care_services.exposure: Minor gender-affirming care banned except narrow dysphoria diagnosis; adult insurance exclusion reinstated on appeal in 2026; discovery of trans status in emergency or pharmacy settings carries denial risk.
care_services.protection: No documented visitor-specific care denial; challenges pending; national employment-discrimination ruling unaffected in care settings.
care_services.interaction: Care exposure is chiefly resident-facing; a visitor needing emergency or prescription services may face discretionary refusal or invasive verification rather than statutory bar.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy lists 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priority targets for rapid neutralisation; justice-department reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; directives to investigate schools and prosecute teachers supporting a minor's transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy text says powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined; hate-crime statute covers gender identity nationally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises the odds that advocacy, online content or visible trans presentation draws investigative rather than protective attention, amplifying other exposures.

minors_guardians.exposure: Binary-sex facilities statute reaches a trans minor in restrooms, locker rooms and dormitories; a bill requiring school staff to out trans students passed both chambers; minor care ban in force.
minors_guardians.protection: Outing bill's final disposition unresolved; court injunctions on some national measures; no documented enforcement against a visiting minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces facility exclusion at state buildings and heightened risk of official inquiry, with school-outing provisions mostly irrelevant to a short-stay visitor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-level trans-specific violence data sourced; 37 states lacked gender-identity bias statutes as of 2019; enforcement posture of local police toward trans complainants undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 23 states cover it in bias statutes; no sodomy law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of data in a well-documented jurisdiction is a weak positive, but the state's repeal-threatened local ordinances leave thin practical recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide gender-identity discrimination protection; religious-refusal immunity; nullification of city ordinances pending; no sourced arrest or penalty under the state facilities statute, so enforcement latitude is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National litigation ongoing, legal-aid FAQ, fifteen municipal ordinances, national hate-crime statute.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist on paper nationally but do not reach the facility, service-denial or custody exposures a visitor would actually encounter in this state.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor bars detention for marker discrepancy and only denies entry after intrusive questioning. Here entry refusal is compounded by possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and the destination state imposes universal facility exclusion by birth sex with no remedy, plus documented custodial harm — materially worse.

That anchor shows two-day detention, mockery, coerced statements and threats of prison, but no statutory exclusion regime or documented systemic custody abuse. This case is similar in official-discretion severity but adds tier-1 facility exclusion and state-perpetrated custodial harm, placing it just below.

That anchor has an ombudsman whose charter actually secures release and bars prolonged holds. Here no working remedy reaches the facilities statute or custody practice; protections are paper or judicially contested, so this case sits far lower.

parsed.synthesis: A visitor who is outed encounters a stacked regime: border officers may treat a marker mismatch as suspected deception, with refusal and possible permanent ineligibility; the destination state's binary-sex statute excludes trans people from restrooms, locker rooms, dormitories and shelters with no state-level antidiscrimination remedy and a religious-refusal immunity permitting service denial; and any arrest or immigration hold places the traveller in birth-sex custody where conversion-style practices and reported abuse are documented. National hate-crime coverage, enjoined executive orders and pending litigation are real but do not operate at the points of exposure, leaving a High Risk profile above the denial-of-entry-only anchors and below jurisdictions where protections demonstrably function.
